tier_reason: The benchmark_url (arXiv 2411.05009, CARLA 2024 preprint) is EGRESS_BLOCKED, as are the themoonlight.io review and the TEC orion publication page; two WebSearch snippets of the paper repeat the 1.4x (Kabre, Xeon Gold 6354), 1.6x (Raven, Xeon Platinum 8360Y) and 100% vs 67% performance-portability figures, but compiler, flags and benchmark code were not seen, so snippet-only evidence stays at C. The paper is a peer-reviewed proceedings preprint, so it could reach B once the PDF is opened (paper-access retier candidate).

corrections.caveats: Snippet only: arxiv.org, themoonlight.io and orion.tec.ac.cr are blocked in this environment, so the numbers come from web search summaries of 'A Study of Performance Portability in Plasma Physics Simulations' (Ruzicka, Asch, Meneses, Rampp, Laure; CARLA 2024 proceedings preprint) and could not be checked against the paper's tables; compiler, flags and benchmark code were not seen. The comparison is application-level (one PIC code, a Kokkos port against its own OpenMP variant) and the paper credits Kokkos's automatic memory layout and data-access patterns, not its scheduler; a snippet also says the OpenMP code had been converted to one-dimensional arrays for GPU offload and that this variant underperformed on CPUs, so the CPU win may partly measure a GPU-oriented data layout in the OpenMP baseline (unverified which OpenMP variant the CPU rows used). Other third-party studies report Kokkos overheads of 13-18% (ocean model, CPU) and about 70% of native CUDA throughput (CMS pixel reconstruction), so Kokkos is not generally faster than native code. It is a performance-portability programming model rather than a thread pool, so the thread-pools-work-stealing category is a loose fit. The repo's own core/perf_test and benchmarks/ directories (stream, gups, launch_latency, atomic, ...) publish no result tables. The README still names 5.1.0 as current, but the releases page shows v5.2.2 (2026-09-10); last commit 2026-10-07 from the develop branch commit feed.

notes: Kokkos core is not yet listed (only kokkos-kernels, wave 8, sparse-and-solvers), so not a duplicate. Shortcomings for the orchestrator: snippet-only evidence from a blocked arXiv paper; application-level PIC comparison whose gain is credited to data layout, with an OpenMP baseline that may use a GPU-oriented 1D-array layout on CPU; no compiler or flags seen; loose category fit.
